added_lemmas.statement: The corrected Gaussian family in \(\texttt{def:primitive-gaussian-family}\), restricted to any compact neighborhood on which its bridge and fixed-role variance inequalities are strict, is a stationary independent-over-time, one-factor, square proximal synthetic-control subclass satisfying Shi et al.'s Assumptions 1--5, supplementary conditions D.1--D.10, and the fixed-role full-rank condition for either predeclared role.  The same conclusion holds row by row for a diagonal constant-effect family in which the donor and supplemental-proxy measurement errors are independent conditional on the factor and the exceptional centered rare-jump variable occurs only in the treated unit's idiosyncratic untreated-outcome error.  Hence the reduced-form class \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) is not asserted to contain, or to be contained in, the full published class; rather, these explicit laws belong to their intersection.  Consequently, any coverage or impossibility property proved separately for these laws also holds within every published class containing this subclass.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We verify the published-model conditions directly.  First consider a fixed row of the corrected family.  Write
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}=e_{0t}+\xi_t,\qquad
 \varepsilon_{1t}=c_1e_{1t},\qquad
 \varepsilon_{2t}=c_{2,n}e_{2t}.
\]
The observed untreated outcomes have the one-factor representation
\[
 Y_t(0)=1\cdot F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},\qquad
 W_{1t}=c_1F_t+\varepsilon_{1t},\qquad
 W_{2t}=c_{2,n}F_t+\varepsilon_{2t}.
\]
The three errors are mutually independent conditional on \(F_t\), because all five primitive Gaussian coordinates in the corrected construction are mutually independent.  This proves the required donor--proxy conditional independence and the corresponding exclusion condition for either exchange of the two control roles.  Consistency holds by construction: the observed treated outcome is \(Y_t(0)\) before treatment and \(Y_t(0)+\tau\) afterward, with no anticipation.  The treatment effect is the constant \(\Delta_t=\tau\), so the causal estimand is not introduced through an observed moment:
\[
 \mathbb E_n\Delta_t=\mathbb E_n\tau=\tau.
\]

For role \(j\), the scalar synthetic-control loading is \(\alpha_j=1/c_j\), because
\[
 c_j\alpha_j=1.
\]
For the opposite role \(k\), independence and \(B=\mathbb E_nF_t^2>0\) give
\[
 M_s=\mathbb E_n(W_{kt}W_{jt})
     =c_kc_jB>0,
\qquad
 \mathbb E_n\{W_{kt}Y_t(0)\}=c_kB=M_s\alpha_j.
\]
Thus the bridge exists, is unique, and has full row rank.  Its residual is
\[
 Y_t(0)-W_{jt}\alpha_j=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{jt},
\]
which is centered.  Adding the constant treatment effect and taking expectations yields
\[
 \mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{jt}\alpha_j\}
 =\tau+\mathbb E_n(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{jt})=\tau.
\]
This proves, rather than defines, the relation between the causal target and the published fixed-role identifying moment.

All observable coordinates are independent and identically distributed over \(t\).  They are therefore strictly stationary and ergodic, their absolute-regularity coefficients vanish after lag zero, and their pre- and post-treatment residual processes have absolutely summable covariance sequences.  Gaussian laws are dominated by Lebesgue measure and have moments of every finite order.  On a compact parameter neighborhood bounded away from
\[
 f=0,\quad b=0,\quad x=0,\quad y=0,\quad \zeta=0,\quad
 t_1=0,\quad t_2=0,\quad M_s=0,
\]
the Gaussian moments possess one common integrable envelope.  The moment maps are polynomials in the data and continuously differentiable in the finite-dimensional bridge and ATT parameters.  Their population bridge derivative is
\[
 -\mathbb E_n(W_{kt}W_{jt})=-M_s\neq0,
\]
and their ATT derivative is \(-1\).  The resulting fixed-role Jacobian is triangular with nonzero diagonal and hence nonsingular.  The law of large numbers gives sample-Jacobian convergence.

For a fixed role, the pre-period bridge score is \(W_{kt}(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{jt})\) and the post-period ATT residual is \(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{jt}\).  Their respective variances are strictly positive because
\[
 \mathbb E_n(W_{kt}^2)>0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{jt})
 =b+\zeta+\operatorname{Var}(e_{jt})>0,
\]
and the two time blocks are disjoint.  Hence the fixed-role limiting moment covariance is positive definite even though the covariance obtained by stacking both roles may be singular.  The assumed limit \(n/m\to r\in(0,\infty)\) supplies comparable horizons.  Compactness of a sufficiently small closed neighborhood of the true finite-dimensional parameter, together with the strict Jacobian, variance, and rank inequalities just verified, supplies the remaining compactness, identification, domination, derivative, covariance, and full-rank requirements in supplementary conditions D.1--D.10.

The diagonal family in the maximal-failure theorem has the same one-factor equations.  In an ordinary row its treated idiosyncratic error is Gaussian.  In row \(q\), it is
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}^{(q)}
 =I_{q,t}-p_q+a_qZ_{0t},
 \qquad p_q=q^{-2},\qquad a_q=q^{-4},
\]
where \(I_{q,t}\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(p_q\), and \(Z_{0t}\) is independent standard normal.  This error is centered, has a strictly positive Lebesgue density because \(a_q>0\), has moments of every finite order, and is independent of the factor and of both Gaussian measurement errors.  The two measurement-error variances in that row are \(a_q^2>0\).  Thus every fixed row retains domination, conditional proxy independence, positive fixed-role covariance, and nonsingular Jacobian and bridge rank.  All rows are independent and identically distributed over time, treatment remains \(\Delta_t=\tau\), and the horizons are comparable.  The same calculations therefore verify the published assumptions row by row for the diagonal family.

These checks establish an explicit common subclass.  They do not prove a set inclusion between the paper's whole reduced-form class and Shi et al.'s full class: the former imposes geometric beta mixing and permits a singular covariance after stacking roles, whereas the latter contains structural interactive-effects and fixed-role conditions not imposed throughout \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\).  Any result established separately on the displayed common subclass transfers upward to a class containing it, and the corrected primitive Gaussian points inherit the same published-class interpretation.

added_lemmas.statement:
The asserted whole-array uniform selector-conditional convergence is false under \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), and its failure can be maximal even inside the stationary independent-over-time square subclass satisfying Shi et al.'s Assumptions 1--5, supplementary conditions D.1--D.10, and the fixed-role full-rank condition for both predeclared roles.  Specifically, fix
\[
 0<\kappa<\frac{6373}{15369},\qquad
 0<\nu<\frac{39}{625},
\]
and a sufficiently large finite moment envelope.  For every sufficiently large integer \(q\), there is a whole triangular array \((P_j^{(q)})_{j\geq1}\in\mathcal M(0)\) with constant treatment effect \(\Delta_t=\tau\), conditionally independent factor-measurement errors, and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{39}{625},\qquad
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1\quad(s\in\mathcal S),
\]
whose stacked limiting covariance is singular, but for
\[
 T_q=
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
      {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
\]
one has
\[
 \lim_{q\to\infty}
 \mathbb E_{P_q^{(q)}}\!\left[
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
  \left|
   \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}\{T_q\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A\}-\Phi(x)
  \right|
 \right]=1.
\]
Thus positive limiting marginal variances, coordinatewise studentization, a logarithm-squared mixing gap, and singular-covariance-safe Gaussian mapping do not yield whole-array uniform inference without a uniform finite-row variance and distributional-stabilization condition.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We construct and verify the arrays.  Let
\[
 B_0=\frac{6373}{30000},\qquad
 x_0=\frac18,\qquad
 \bar b_0=\frac78,\qquad
 t_0=\frac{5123}{10000},\qquad
 c_0=t_0^{-1/2}.
\]
These constants were chosen so that
\[
 t_0+B_0+x_0=4B_0,\qquad
 \eta_0=\frac{B_0}{t_0+B_0+x_0}=\frac14,
\qquad
 \frac{B_0}{t_0}=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa.
\]
Set \(m_j=j\), so \(j/m_j=1\) and the sample-ratio condition holds with \(r=1\).

For each sufficiently large \(q\), define a whole array \((P_j^{(q)})_{j\geq1}\).  Every row is independent and identically distributed over the two-sided time index.  In every ordinary row \(j\neq q\), generate mutually independent
\[
 F_t\sim N(0,B_0),\qquad
 e_{1t},e_{2t}\sim N(0,x_0),\qquad
 \varepsilon_{0t}\sim N(0,\bar b_0),
\]
and put
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},\qquad
 \Delta_t=\tau,\qquad
 W_{1t}=c_0(F_t+e_{1t}),\qquad
 W_{2t}=c_0(F_t+e_{2t}).
\]
Role one uses \(W_1\) as donor and \(W_2\) as proxy; role two exchanges them.  The Gaussian treated error can, if desired, be split as the sum of two independent \(N(0,7/16)\) coordinates, exactly matching the corrected primitive parameterization.

In the exceptional row \(j=q\), retain \(F_t\sim N(0,B_0)\), let
\[
 p_q=q^{-2},\qquad a_q=q^{-4},
\]
and generate mutually independent
\[
 I_{q,t}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_q),\qquad
 Z_{0t},Z_{1t},Z_{2t}\sim N(0,1).
\]
Define
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}=I_{q,t}-p_q+a_qZ_{0t},\qquad
 e_{1t}=a_qZ_{1t},\qquad e_{2t}=a_qZ_{2t},
\]
and use the same formulas for \(Y_t(0)\), \(\Delta_t\), and \(W_{jt}\).  Thus the exceptional centered skewness lies in the untreated treated-unit error, never in the treatment effect.  Conditional on \(F_t\), the treated error and the two measurement errors are mutually independent.  The causal target is
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_j^{(q)}}\Delta_t=\tau
\]
in every row, while the observed post-treatment residual mean equals this target by the bridge calculation below.

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M(0)\).  Independence over time implies strict stationarity and beta-mixing coefficients equal to zero at every positive lag.  The Gaussian coordinates have fixed moments, \(0\leq I_{q,t}\leq1\), and \(p_q,a_q\leq1\); consequently, for every fixed \(\delta_0>0\),
\[
 \sup_q\sup_j
 \mathbb E_{P_j^{(q)}}\|X_t\|^{8+\delta_0}<\infty.
\]
Choose \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) larger than this finite bound.

For either role and every row, independence and centering give
\[
 M_s=\mathbb E(Z_{s,t}W_{D_s,t})=c_0^2B_0
     =\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\{Z_{s,t}Y_t(0)\}=c_0B_0=M_s/c_0.
\]
Since this scalar moment is nonzero, the bridge definition gives
\[
 \alpha_s=\frac1{c_0},
\qquad
 Y_t(0)-W_{D_s,t}\alpha_s=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{s,t},
\]
where \(e_{s,t}\) denotes the selected donor's measurement error.  The last residual is centered, proving bridge centering.  With constant treatment,
\[
 \mathbb E\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{D_s,t}\alpha_s\}
 =\tau,
\]
so the observed identifying moment equals the separately defined causal target.

Both donor variables have the same distribution within every row.  Hence their population ridge coefficients and minimized population losses agree, so
\[
 L_{1,j}=L_{2,j},\qquad
 \sup_{j\geq1}\sqrt j\,|L_{1,j}-L_{2,j}|=0.
\]
This verifies the bounded-gap condition with \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}=0\).

It remains to calculate the limiting variances.  Since each donor mean is zero, \(\mu_s=0\), so \(H_s=0\), \(\psi_{s,t}=0\), and \(A_s=0\) for both roles.  In every ordinary row, the tied scalar formula from the corrected primitive construction applies with
\[
 B=B_0,\qquad x=y=x_0,\qquad
 \bar b=\bar b_0,\qquad \eta=\eta_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(D)
 &=4\eta_0^2\{(1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0\}(2x_0)
   +4\eta_0^4x_0^2\\
 &=\frac{39}{625}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For transparency, the exact cancellation is
\[
 (1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0
 =\frac{159119}{160000},
\]
and substitution of \(B_0=6373/30000\), \(x_0=1/8\), and \(\eta_0=1/4\) gives the displayed rational value.  The post residuals in an ordinary row are
\[
 v_{1,t}=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{1t},\qquad
 v_{2,t}=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{2t},
\]
so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(R_s)=\bar b_0+x_0=1,
\qquad
 V_s=\operatorname{Var}(A_s)+r\operatorname{Var}(R_s)=1>\nu.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:gap-variance-inheritance}\), \(V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1\), because \(\operatorname{Var}(A_s)=0\).  The stacked limiting covariance is singular because both pre-ATT coordinates vanish identically.

For each fixed \(q\), all rows after \(q\) have the same ordinary law.  Thus the exceptional row cannot alter the array's limiting long-run covariance.  The centered score vector in an ordinary row is a degree-two Gaussian polynomial and has a finite third moment.  For any coefficient vector \(a\), if \(G_t\) denotes that centered score vector and \(\Sigma_G\) its covariance, Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left\{\frac{\mathrm i a^\prime G_t}{\sqrt j}\right\}
 =1-\frac{a^\prime\Sigma_Ga}{2j}+O(j^{-3/2}).
\]
Independence over \(t\) and raising this expression to the \(j\)-th power yield
\[
 \exp\!\left(-\frac12a^\prime\Sigma_Ga\right).
\]
This Cramér--Wold calculation proves covariance convergence and the possibly singular joint Gaussian limit without any covariance inversion.  We have verified every defining condition of \(\mathcal M(0)\).  The rowwise published-class inclusion follows from \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\): the factor errors are conditionally independent, the bridge is scalar and full rank, treatment is constant, and the exceptional error has a positive Gaussian-convolution density and finite moments.

We now analyze row \(q\).  Let \(\mathcal N_q\) be the event that \(I_{q,t}=0\) for every \(t\) in the late bridge-fitting block \(\mathcal B_q\) and post block \(\mathcal C_q\).  Since their total length is at most \(2q\),
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal N_q)\geq(1-p_q)^{2q}
 =(1-q^{-2})^{2q}\longrightarrow1.
\]
This event is independent of the early sigma-field \(\mathcal F_A\).  The selected label is \(\mathcal F_A\)-measurable, and the following bounds hold for both labels.

Let \(j\) denote the donor chosen by a fixed role and \(k\neq j\) its proxy.  On \(\mathcal N_q\), the true bridge residual on both retained blocks is
\[
 r_{j,t}^0=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{j,t}
 =-p_q+a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt}).
\]
Writing empirical averages over \(\mathcal B_q\) with a bar and
\[
 \widehat M_{j,q}
 =|\mathcal B_q|^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_q}W_{kt}W_{jt},
\]
the sample bridge equation gives the exact identity
\[
 \widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j
 =\widehat M_{j,q}^{-1}
   |\mathcal B_q|^{-1}
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal B_q}W_{kt}r_{j,t}^0.
\]
Because \(|\mathcal B_q|/q\to1-\varrho>0\),
\[
 \widehat M_{j,q}=c_0^2B_0+O_P(q^{-1/2}),
\qquad
 \overline W_{k,\mathcal B_q}=O_P(q^{-1/2}).
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal N_q\), the centered Gaussian part of
\(W_{kt}r_{j,t}^0\) has standard deviation \(O(a_q)\), while its constant part is \(-p_qW_{kt}\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j
 =O_P\!\left(\frac{p_q+a_q}{\sqrt q}\right)
\]
uniformly over the two roles.  The post donor mean satisfies
\[
 \overline W_{j,\mathcal C_q}=O_P(q^{-1/2}).
\]
Consequently the definition of the gap-split estimator yields, on \(\mathcal N_q\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau
 &=\overline r^0_{j,\mathcal C_q}
   -(\widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j)
     \overline W_{j,\mathcal C_q}\\
 &=-p_q+O_P(a_q q^{-1/2})
   +O_P\{(p_q+a_q)q^{-1}\}\\
 &=-p_q\{1+o_P(1)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

We next bound the actual Bartlett denominator.  For any centered scalar observations \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\), the Bartlett estimator with bandwidth \(h\) satisfies, by Cauchy--Schwarz and weights bounded by one,
\[
 0\leq\widehat\Omega_g
 \leq(2h+1)N^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Ng_t^2.
\]
The fitted centered post residual differs from \(a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt})\) by
\(-(\widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j)W_{jt}\) and a sample-centering term.  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{v,j}
 =O_P\!\left[
 h_q\left\{a_q^2+\frac{(p_q+a_q)^2}{q}\right\}
 \right].
\]
The fitted bridge sensitivity contains the estimated donor mean and obeys
\[
 \widehat H_j=O_P(q^{-1/2}).
\]
The fitted bridge score before multiplication by \(\widehat H_j\) has conditional second moment \(O_P(p_q^2+a_q^2)\).  Applying the same Bartlett bound gives
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{\psi,j}
 =O_P\!\left\{\frac{h_q(p_q^2+a_q^2)}q\right\}.
\]
Since \(|\mathcal B_q|\asymp q\), \(m_q=q\), and \(h_q=O(q^{1/5})\), the standard-error definition implies
\[
 \widehat{\operatorname{se}}_j^2
 =O_P\!\left\{
 \frac{h_qa_q^2}{q}
 +\frac{h_qp_q^2}{q^2}
 \right\}.
\]
With \(p_q=q^{-2}\) and \(a_q=q^{-4}\),
\[
 \frac{\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_j}{p_q}
 =O_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{h_qa_q^2}{qp_q^2}
       +\frac{h_q}{q^2}\right\}^{1/2}
 \right]=o_P(1).
\]
Because \(a_q>0\), the fitted residual vector has a nonzero continuous Gaussian component.  The finite Bartlett kernel matrix is positive definite for \(h_q<m_q\), so the post Bartlett quadratic form, and hence the selected standard error, is strictly positive almost surely.  Combining the last two displays with the numerator expansion proves
\[
 T_q\longrightarrow-\infty
\]
in probability on \(\mathcal N_q\), uniformly over the two possible early-selected labels.  Since \(\Pr(\mathcal N_q)\to1\), the same divergence holds unconditionally and after averaging the conditional law given \(\mathcal F_A\).

Choose a deterministic sequence \(b_q\to\infty\) slowly enough that
\[
 \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}(T_q>-b_q)\longrightarrow0.
\]
For the conditional Kolmogorov distance \(K_q\), evaluation at the moving point \(-b_q\), followed by Jensen's inequality, gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E K_q
 &\geq
 \mathbb E\left|
  \Pr\{T_q\leq-b_q\mid\mathcal F_A\}-\Phi(-b_q)
 \right|\\
 &\geq
 \left|
  \Pr(T_q\leq-b_q)-\Phi(-b_q)
 \right|
 \longrightarrow1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every Kolmogorov distance is at most one, so \(\mathbb E K_q\to1\).  This is the maximal possible failure and, in particular, implies the weaker lower bound in the theorem it replaces.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \(\theta=(\mu,f,b,x,y,\zeta,r,t_1,t_2)\in\Theta_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{leg}}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R\), put
\[
 \bar b=b+\zeta,\qquad B=\mu^2+f,\qquad
 R=t_1+B+x,\qquad \eta=B/R,\qquad K=\mu/B,
\]
\[
 c_1=t_1^{-1/2},\qquad
 t_{2,n}=t_2-\frac{R^2}{B^2}\frac d{\sqrt n},
 \qquad c_{2,n}=t_{2,n}^{-1/2}.
\]
Generate mutually independent coordinates
\[
 F_t\sim N(\mu,f),\quad e_{0t}\sim N(0,b),\quad
 e_{1t}\sim N(0,x),\quad e_{2t}\sim N(0,y),\quad
 \xi_t\sim N(0,\zeta),
\]
independently over \(t\), and define
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+e_{0t}+\xi_t,\qquad
 \Delta_t=\tau,\qquad
 W_{1t}=c_1(F_t+e_{1t}),\qquad
 W_{2t}=c_{2,n}(F_t+e_{2t}).
\]
Role one uses \(W_{1t}\) as donor and \(W_{2t}\) as supplemental proxy, while role two exchanges those assignments.  Thus, conditional on \(F_t\), the treated idiosyncratic error \(e_{0t}+\xi_t\) and the two factor-measurement errors are mutually independent, and the causal target satisfies \(\mathbb E_n\Delta_t=\tau\).

The tied manifold is \(t_2=t_1+x-y>0\).  Along the displayed local calibration, \(t_{2,n}>0\) eventually, both bridge matrices equal \(c_1c_{2,n}B\), the bridge coefficients are \(1/c_1\) and \(1/c_{2,n}\), and
\[
 \sqrt n(L_1-L_2)=d+O(n^{-1/2}).
\]
At the tied limit,
\[
 \sigma_D^2
 =4\eta^2\{(1-\eta)^2B+\bar b\}(x+y)
  +2\eta^4(x^2+y^2),
\]
\[
 c_{D1}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_1)
 =-2\eta K\{(1-\eta)Bx+\bar b y\},
\qquad
 c_{D2}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_2)
 =2\eta K\{(1-\eta)By+\bar b x\},
\]
and, because treatment is constant,
\[
 V_1=K^2(B+y)(\bar b+x)+r(\bar b+x),
\qquad
 V_2=K^2(B+x)(\bar b+y)+r(\bar b+y).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \Gamma(\theta,d)
 =\left(
 -\frac d{\sigma_D},
 \frac{c_{D1}}{\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_1}},
 \frac{c_{D2}}{\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_2}},
 V_1,V_2
 \right).
\]
The corrected family \(\mathcal G\) is the collection of these constant-treatment local Gaussian arrays.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The directed published-class repair requires constant treatment. The independent xi coordinate therefore belongs in the treated unit's untreated-outcome error, so its variance combines with b. This changes the ATT variances and selector covariances while preserving the local ridge-loss construction.

proposed_core_edits.name: cD1
proposed_core_edits.reason: After xi is moved from the treatment effect into the untreated treated-unit error, its variance zeta enters the role-one selector--ATT covariance through the total treated-error variance b+zeta.

proposed_core_edits.name: cD2
proposed_core_edits.reason: After xi is moved from the treatment effect into the untreated treated-unit error, its variance zeta enters the role-two selector--ATT covariance through the total treated-error variance b+zeta.

The existing one-half lower bound is obsolete. The same quantifier obstruction admits a constant-effect published-class witness whose expected conditional Kolmogorov distance converges to the maximal value one.

proposed.comparator_claim: For a predetermined donor/proxy partition, the structural proximal synthetic-control assumptions identify the bridge and support fixed-role GMM/HAC inference.
Conditioning a Gaussian linear statistic on a polyhedral selection event yields an exact truncated-normal pivot and conditional confidence interval.
Explicit Gaussian formulas characterize coverage of naive and protected intervals after selection between two nested regression models.
Even functionals are invariant under the paper's skew-symmetric perturbation construction.
Separated-block sample splitting is asymptotically valid for broad beta-mixing time-series functionals under stability conditions.
Kernel long-run covariance estimators are consistent under serial dependence and suitable bandwidth growth.
Section 5, Theorem 3 establishes asymptotic normality of the article's doubly robust GMM estimator when at least one of its two bridge models is correctly specified.
For a fixed proximal proxy structure, influence functions, semiparametric efficiency bounds, and locally efficient estimators are characterized.
Simultaneous protection over all candidate submodels guarantees post-selection coverage under arbitrary selection rules.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The relation to Shi et al. is an explicit common-subclass transfer, not a strict tightening over their full published class. The complete comparator table must record that corrected positioning.

prose_updates.tldr: Two valid proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet produce a nonregular conventional interval when the role with smaller pre-period ridge loss is reported. The conventional interval has a selected-Gaussian limit and an exact coverage function: every exact selector tie protects every symmetric Wald level, all local gaps are protected exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared selector correlations, and the strict error sign is the gap sign times their squared-correlation difference. A constant-treatment, conditionally independent one-factor Gaussian chart realizes both regimes inside a stationary square subclass of the published Shi et al. model; its asymmetric point has limiting coverage \(0.8857757910650707\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval, with strict undercoverage on a relatively open neighborhood. Early selection, a logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fitting, post residual averaging, and Bartlett studentization do not by themselves yield uniform selector-conditional normality over the declared whole-array reduced-form class: an explicit published-class diagonal witness makes the expected conditional Kolmogorov distance converge to one. Uniform validity therefore requires an additional uniform finite-row variance and distributional-stabilization condition.

project_justification.gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and supplemental-proxy roles, while general selective-inference theory does not characterize unconditional ordinary symmetric-Wald coverage when a pre-period loss comparison switches the reported ATT coordinate. Nor do pointwise fixed-role limit conditions alone justify a whole-array uniform guarantee for a time-split redesign.
project_justification.niche: The binary ridge selector has enough Gaussian geometry for an exact if-and-only-if coverage frontier, while its covariance coordinates remain interpretable through proximal bridge Jacobians, donor means, and long-run residual variation. A stationary independent-over-time constant-effect subclass provides a precise bridge to the published Shi et al. assumptions without claiming that the paper's full reduced-form class and their full structural class contain one another.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the selected limit, evaluable coverage map, squared-correlation frontier and strict sign rule, a continuous constant-effect primitive realization with open strict miscoverage, and a maximal uniform-failure converse for the proposed split procedure. The converse pinpoints the missing design requirement: any uniform selector-conditional theorem must add uniform finite-row variance and distributional stabilization beyond limiting marginal variance margins.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each bridge is estimated from pre-treatment moments. The conventional procedure uses all \(n\) pre-period observations for both role selection and bridge fitting, substitutes fitted bridge Jacobians, post donor means, bridge coefficients, and ATT residuals, and uses separate pre- and post-period Bartlett estimates with bandwidth \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). The redesigned candidate selects early, discards a logarithm-squared gap, fits the selected bridge late, averages its post residuals, and uses Bartlett bandwidth \(h_n=\lfloor\min(|\mathcal B_n|,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). These operations remove direct selection--estimation reuse, but they do not establish uniform selector-conditional normality over the present whole-array class without additional rowwise stabilization.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi et al. (2026) provide the causal and inferential anchor: consistency, an interactive-effects untreated-outcome model, synthetic-control loading balance, conditional proxy independence, and fixed-role long-panel GMM/HAC conditions. The present abstract theory instead uses a reduced-form square unconditional bridge-moment class with geometric beta mixing and permits singular covariance after stacking roles; neither complete class is claimed to contain the other. An explicit stationary independent-over-time, constant-effect one-factor subclass satisfies Shi et al.'s Assumptions 1--5, supplementary conditions D.1--D.10, and both fixed-role rank requirements, so the primitive miscoverage example and the uniform-failure converse transfer through a proved intersection witness. Lee et al. (2016) supply Gaussian half-space conditioning for an exact conditional selective pivot. Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015) give comparator-specific post-selection coverage calculations in nested regression, while Azzalini and Regoli (2012) explain even-function Gaussian symmetry; neither source gives the proximal switched-coordinate squared-correlation frontier. Lunde (2019) and Andrews (1991) motivate separated-block mixing arguments and Bartlett HAC, but the diagonal theorem shows that those devices need uniform rowwise stabilization before they support the paper's desired whole-array claim. Qiu et al. (2024) and Cui et al. (2024) remain fixed-role proximal GMM and influence-function comparators rather than role-selection results.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian coverage algebra, constant-effect primitive covariance map, numerical integral, and maximal diagonal counterexample are complete calculations. What is not supplied is a positive uniform theorem for the split estimator on a strengthened class. Pointwise covariance convergence and positive limiting marginal variances leave the evaluation row unrestricted; the diagonal array exploits that gap while satisfying every stated whole-array condition and the published fixed-role assumptions row by row. A future positive result must formulate a uniform finite-row lower variance bound together with a uniform Gaussian or self-normalized distributional approximation and uniform Bartlett consistency. Generic time splitting and singular-covariance-safe coordinatewise studentization remain supporting machinery, not the paper's novelty.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact coverage theorem concerns two predeclared square bridge systems, ridge penalty one, stationary geometrically beta-mixing panels, fixed high-moment and bridge-rank radii, bounded root-\(n\) selector gaps, and positive limiting ATT and selector-contrast variance margins. The conventional interval uses the full pre-period sample for selection and bridge fitting and a fitted-score Bartlett standard error. The primitive chart now has constant treatment effect and independent factor-measurement errors; its two displayed points and the diagonal impossibility witness lie in a stationary square subclass satisfying the published Shi et al. fixed-role assumptions. This intersection witness is not an unqualified extension to Shi et al.'s full class. The early-select, logarithm-squared-gap, late-fit proposal remains a useful design template, but uniform selector-conditional normality is false over \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) as defined; a valid uniform theorem must impose and verify an additional finite-row stabilization condition. The analysis does not cover the rectangular simplex-constrained donor/proxy rule in the West-German application, estimate the local population loss drift, recover full-pre-period efficiency after splitting, or solve selection among three or more roles. For the application, the actionable recommendation is a predeclared two-candidate robustness analysis before retaining the reported negative GDP conclusion.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 e_{0t}^{\star}=e_{0t}+\xi_t,
 \qquad
 \bar b=\operatorname{Var}(e_{0t}^{\star})=b+\zeta.
\]
By the corrected construction in \(\texttt{def:primitive-gaussian-family}\), \(e_{0t}^{\star}\), \(e_{1t}\), \(e_{2t}\), and \(F_t\) are mutually independent except for the deterministic means already specified, and
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+e_{0t}^{\star},
 \qquad
 \Delta_t=\tau.
\]
Thus the causal estimand and the constant treatment effect agree because
\[
 \mathbb E_n[\Delta_t]=\mathbb E_n[\tau]=\tau.
\]
All coordinates have full Gaussian support on their respective Euclidean spaces, all moments are finite, and the process is independent and identically distributed over \(t\); in particular, it is strictly stationary and its beta-mixing coefficients vanish at every positive lag.

For role one the donor and proxy are, respectively,
\[
 W_{1t}=c_1(F_t+e_{1t}),
 \qquad
 W_{2t}=c_{2,n}(F_t+e_{2t}),
\]
and role two exchanges these assignments.  Put \(B=\mathbb E_nF_t^2=\mu^2+f\).  Independence and centering of the measurement errors give, in either role,
\[
 M_s=c_1c_{2,n}\mathbb E_nF_t^2=c_1c_{2,n}B.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E_n[W_{2t}Y_t(0)]=c_{2,n}B,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_n[W_{1t}Y_t(0)]=c_1B.
\]
Since \(B>0\), \(c_1>0\), and \(c_{2,n}>0\) eventually, the scalar bridge matrices are invertible and the bridge definition yields
\[
 \alpha_1=\frac{c_{2,n}B}{c_1c_{2,n}B}=\frac1{c_1},
 \qquad
 \alpha_2=\frac{c_1B}{c_1c_{2,n}B}=\frac1{c_{2,n}}.
\]
It follows pointwise that
\[
 Y_t(0)-W_{1t}\alpha_1=e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{1t},
 \qquad
 Y_t(0)-W_{2t}\alpha_2=e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{2t}.
\]
Both residuals have expectation zero, proving bridge centering for each role rather than assuming it.  The observed post-period residual identifies the causal target because, for \(j\in\{1,2\}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{jt}\alpha_j\}
 =\tau+\mathbb E_n(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{jt})
 =\tau.
\]
This equality is a consequence of the bridge calculation and the constant-effect construction; it is not a definition of the causal target.  At the tied limit, the scalar singular value is
\[
 |M_s|=c_1c_2B=\frac{B}{\sqrt{t_1t_2}}.
\]

We next derive the ridge-loss calibration.  For a generic donor \(W_j=c_j(F+e_j)\), its scalar ridge normal equation is
\[
 \{1+\mathbb E_n(W_j^2)\}a_j=\mathbb E_n\{W_jY_t(0)\}.
\]
Using \(c_j^2=t_j^{-1}\), this gives
\[
 a_j=\frac{c_jB}{1+c_j^2\{B+\operatorname{Var}(e_j)\}},
 \qquad
 W_ja_j=\frac{B}{t_j+B+\operatorname{Var}(e_j)}(F+e_j).
\]
The tied-manifold equality \(t_2=t_1+x-y\) implies
\[
 t_1+B+x=t_2+B+y=R,
\]
so the two ridge predictions have the common loading \(\eta=B/R\).  Substitution of the normal-equation solution into the ridge objective, or equivalently completion of the scalar square, gives
\[
 L_j=\mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)^2\}
     -\frac{B^2}{t_j+B+\operatorname{Var}(e_j)}.
\]
Hence \(L_1=L_2\) at the tied limit.  Let
\[
 \delta_n=\frac{R^2}{B^2}\frac d{\sqrt n},
 \qquad
 t_{2,n}=t_2-\delta_n.
\]
Because \(t_2>0\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), one has \(t_{2,n}>0\) eventually.  The preceding loss formula then gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_1-L_2
 &=\frac{B^2}{R-\delta_n}-\frac{B^2}{R}\\
 &=\frac{B^2\delta_n}{R(R-\delta_n)}\\
 &=\frac d{\sqrt n}\frac{R}{R-\delta_n}
 =\frac d{\sqrt n}+O(n^{-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)=d+O(n^{-1/2})\), and the construction realizes the declared local gap without changing either bridge identity.

We now calculate the limiting covariance map.  At the tied limit define
\[
 U_0=(1-\eta)F+e_0^{\star}.
\]
The two ridge residuals are \(U_0-\eta e_1\) and \(U_0-\eta e_2\).  Since the ridge-penalty difference is \(\eta^2(t_1-t_2)=\eta^2(y-x)\), centering the one-period loss contrast gives
\[
 D_t=-2\eta U_0(e_1-e_2)
     +\eta^2(e_1^2-e_2^2+y-x).
\]
The donor means are \(c_j\mu\).  The definitions \(H_s=-\mu_s^{\prime}M_s^{-1}\) and \(\psi_{s,t}=H_su_{s,t}\) therefore reduce to
\[
 \psi_{1,t}=-K(F_t+e_{2t})(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \psi_{2,t}=-K(F_t+e_{1t})(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{2t}),
 \qquad
 K=\frac\mu B.
\]
Constant treatment and the bridge identities similarly give the post-period residuals
\[
 v_{1,t}=e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{1t},
 \qquad
 v_{2,t}=e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{2t}.
\]
The relevant score vector is a polynomial of degree at most two in Gaussian coordinates and hence has a finite third absolute moment.  For any fixed coefficient vector \(a\), Taylor's formula applied to its centered one-period score \(G_t\) gives, uniformly along the local calibration,
\[
 \mathbb E_n\exp\!\left\{\frac{\mathrm i a^{\prime}G_t}{\sqrt n}\right\}
 =1-\frac{a^{\prime}\Sigma_na}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}),
\]
where \(\Sigma_n=\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(G_t)\) converges to its tied value.  Independence over time and raising the last expression to the \(n\)-th power give the centered Gaussian characteristic function \(\exp(-a^{\prime}\Sigma a/2)\).  The same calculation applies to the post-period sum, and disjoint pre- and post-period samples are independent.  Thus the asserted joint Gaussian coordinates exist, their long-run covariances equal their one-period covariances, and the pre- and post-period Gaussian limits are independent.  This argument permits a singular stacked covariance because it does not invert \(\Sigma\).

The two displayed terms in \(D_t\) are uncorrelated: after expansion, every cross term contains an odd centered Gaussian moment.  Also
\[
 \mathbb E_n(U_0^2)=(1-\eta)^2B+\bar b,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_n\{(e_1-e_2)^2\}=x+y,
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(e_1^2-e_2^2)=2(x^2+y^2).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sigma_D^2
 =4\eta^2\{(1-\eta)^2B+\bar b\}(x+y)
  +2\eta^4(x^2+y^2).
\]
For the role-one selector covariance, condition first on \((F,e_0^{\star})\).  Direct expansion and the independence of \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_n[(e_1-e_2)(F+e_2)(e_0^{\star}-e_1)
        \mid F,e_0^{\star}]
 =-xF-ye_0^{\star}.
\]
The quadratic part of \(D_t\) has zero covariance with \(\psi_{1,t}\), again because its expanded terms contain odd centered Gaussian moments.  Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c_{D1}
 &=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_1)\\
 &=-2\eta K\{(1-\eta)Bx+\bar b y\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The same calculation after exchanging roles gives
\[
 c_{D2}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_2)
 =2\eta K\{(1-\eta)By+\bar b x\}.
\]
In each pre-score product, its two factors are independent.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(A_1)=K^2(B+y)(\bar b+x),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(A_2)=K^2(B+x)(\bar b+y).
\]
The post variances are
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(R_1)=\bar b+x,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(R_2)=\bar b+y.
\]
Using the definition \(V_s=\operatorname{Var}(A_s)+r\operatorname{Var}(R_s)\), we obtain
\[
 V_1=K^2(B+y)(\bar b+x)+r(\bar b+x),
 \qquad
 V_2=K^2(B+x)(\bar b+y)+r(\bar b+y),
\]
and, since \(\sigma_D^2>0\) and \(V_s>0\) at the points below,
\[
 \rho_s=\frac{c_{Ds}}{\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_s}}.
\]

At \(\theta_0\), \(\bar b=1\), \(B=2\), \(R=4\), and \(\eta=K=1/2\).  Substitution into the formulas just proved gives
\[
 \sigma_D^2=\frac{13}{4},
 \qquad
 c_{D1}=-1,
 \qquad
 c_{D2}=1,
 \qquad
 V_1=V_2=\frac32+2r.
\]
Thus \(\rho_1=-\rho_2\).  Put \(Z_s=A_s+\sqrt rR_s\).  Because the post limit is independent of \(X=D/\sigma_D\), Gaussian regression of the pre coordinate on \(X\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E(Z_s\mid X)=\frac{c_{Ds}}{\sigma_D}X.
\]
Integration by parts under the standard-normal density gives
\[
 \mathbb E[X\mathbf 1\{X\leq k\}]=-\phi(k),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[X\mathbf 1\{X>k\}]=\phi(k).
\]
It follows that, for every finite \(k\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E[Z_1\mathbf 1\{X\leq k\}+Z_2\mathbf 1\{X>k\}]
 &=\frac{c_{D2}-c_{D1}}{\sigma_D}\phi(k)\\
 &=\frac2{\sigma_D}\phi(k)>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus role selection changes the limiting mean even at the symmetric point.  Nevertheless \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\), so \(\texttt{thm:wald-symmetry-frontier}\) gives
\[
 C_z(k)=2\Phi(z)-1
\]
for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) and every \(z>0\).  The bridge singular value equals \(2\), the selector variance equals \(13/4\), and \(V_s=3/2+2r\).  Hence the strict restrictions \(\kappa<2\) and \(\nu<63/200\) imply every rank and variance margin at this point.  The stipulated strict moment bound gives the remaining legality inequality.

At \(\theta_a\), one has \(\bar b=1/10\), \(B=2\), \(R=4\), \(\eta=K=1/2\), and
\[
 \frac{B}{\sqrt{t_1t_2}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{(9/5)(1/5)}}=\frac{10}{3}.
\]
The covariance formulas yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sigma_D^2
 &=\left\{\frac12+\frac1{10}\right\}
   \left\{\frac15+\frac95\right\}
   +\frac18\left\{\frac1{25}+\frac{81}{25}\right\}
 =\frac{161}{100},\\
 c_{D1}
 &=-\frac12\left\{\frac15+\frac9{50}\right\}
 =-\frac{19}{100},\\
 c_{D2}
 &=\frac12\left\{\frac95+\frac1{50}\right\}
 =\frac{91}{100}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The ATT variances are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_1
 &=\frac14\frac{19}{5}\frac3{10}
   +\frac1{10}\frac3{10}
 =\frac{63}{200},\\
 V_2
 &=\frac14\frac{11}{5}\frac{19}{10}
   +\frac1{10}\frac{19}{10}
 =\frac{247}{200}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
In particular, the smallest bridge singular value is \(10/3>\kappa\), the selector variance is \(161/100>\nu\), and the smallest ATT variance is \(63/200>\nu\).  The exact correlations simplify to
\[
 \rho_1=-\frac{19\sqrt2}{\sqrt{10143}}
 =-0.2667997301850519557810\ldots,
 \qquad
 \rho_2=\frac{91\sqrt2}{\sqrt{39767}}
 =0.6453494964281337119128\ldots .
\]
Thus
\[
 \rho_1^2=\frac{722}{10143}
 <\frac{16562}{39767}=\rho_2^2.
\]
When \(d/\sigma_D=-1\), the definition \(k=-d/\sigma_D\) gives \(k=1\).  Substitution of the exact rational covariances into \(\texttt{def:coverage-functional}\), with \(z=\Phi^{-1}(0.95)\), gives
\[
 C_z(1)=0.885775791065070673638760939696\ldots .
\]
This decimal is obtained without simulation by writing \(\Phi(u)=\{1+\operatorname{erf}(u/\sqrt2)\}/2\), evaluating the two resulting one-dimensional integrals with sixty-decimal arithmetic on \([-12,1]\) and \([1,12]\), and repeating after subdivision.  The omitted Gaussian-tail mass is bounded by
\[
 2\Phi(-12)<4\times10^{-33}.
\]
The strict undercoverage conclusion does not depend on numerical quadrature.  Indeed, \(k>0\) and \(\rho_1^2-\rho_2^2<0\), so \(\texttt{thm:wald-symmetry-frontier}\) proves
\[
 C_z(1)-\{2\Phi(z)-1\}<0.
\]
Since \(2\Phi\{\Phi^{-1}(0.95)\}-1=0.9\), this establishes strict undercoverage analytically.

At \(\theta_a\), \(R^2/B^2=4\), and hence the local path is
\[
 t_{2,n}=\frac15-\frac{4d}{\sqrt n}.
\]
It is positive eventually for every finite \(d\).  The bridge matrices, covariance formulas, Gaussian moments, and the map \(\Gamma(\theta,d)\) are continuous on the region where \(t_{2,n}>0\).  At \((\theta_a,d)\), every legality inequality is strict, as are \(k>0\) and \(\rho_1^2<\rho_2^2\).  These inequalities therefore persist on a relatively open neighborhood in the tied parameter manifold crossed with the local-drift coordinate.  The sign part of \(\texttt{thm:wald-symmetry-frontier}\) gives strict undercoverage throughout that neighborhood.  Exchanging labels exchanges the two squared correlations.  Holding the roles fixed and replacing \(d\) by \(-d\) changes the sign of \(k\), so the same theorem gives strict overcoverage.

Finally, the corrected construction is an explicit square subclass of the published proximal synthetic-control model.  Conditional on \(F_t\), the treated error \(e_{0t}^{\star}\), the donor error, and the proxy error are mutually independent for either role; the synthetic-control loading equality is \(1=c_j\alpha_j\), and the fixed-role rank matrix is the nonzero scalar \(M_s=c_1c_2B\).  Treatment is the constant \(\Delta_t=\tau\), and all observable stochastic coordinates are independent and identically distributed over time.  The complete compactness, domination, identification, derivative, positive covariance, pre/post ratio, and fixed-role rank checks for Shi et al.'s Assumptions 1--5 and supplementary conditions D.1--D.10 are proved in \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\).  Applying that proposition to \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_a\), together with the strict margins calculated above, proves the claimed published-class inclusion for both realizations.
